common_name: Alba Plena Heather (Double White Scotch Heather)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean, sandy or peaty soil in full sun; Alba Plena is one of the oldest known double-flowered heather cultivars, in cultivation since before 1900.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, sandy or peaty soil in full sun; Alba Plena bears double white flowers over mid-green foliage on an upright plant, one of the oldest known double-flowered heather cultivars, in cultivation since before 1900. It blooms in late summer like other Calluna vulgaris cultivars and is widely sold through the UK and European heather trade. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a compact, bushy habit, since unsheared heathers become leggy and open over time.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; H.E. Beale is a classic cultivar dating to the 1920s, prized for its long flower spikes.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; H.E. Beale bears unusually long double pink flower spikes over green foliage on an upright plant to 18-24 inches, a classic cultivar in cultivation since the 1920s and one of the most widely grown heathers worldwide. Its long spikes make it an excellent cut flower in addition to its garden value. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a compact, bushy habit.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; County Wicklow is a well-known Irish double-flowered heather cultivar.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; County Wicklow bears double shell-pink flowers over green foliage on a compact mounding plant to about 12 inches, a well-known Irish heather cultivar long established in the European and UK nursery trade. Its compact habit suits a rock garden or heathland-style bed edge where larger heathers would be out of scale. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a compact, bushy habit.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Robert Chapman is one of the most famous tricolor-foliage heather cultivars, introduced in 1958.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Robert Chapman is one of the most celebrated tricolor-foliage heather cultivars, introduced in 1958, with foliage that shifts from gold in spring and summer to vivid orange and red through winter, topped by lavender-purple flowers. The dramatic seasonal foliage color change gives it year-round interest well beyond its bloom period. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a compact, spreading mound.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Firefly's winter foliage color is the main draw of this long-standing cultivar.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Firefly bears emerald-green summer foliage that turns deep red-orange through winter, paired with mauve-pink flowers, a long-standing foliage cultivar valued for extending heather garden color into the cold season. Its compact upright habit to about 12 inches suits a heathland-style bed or mixed acid-soil border. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a tidy, compact shape.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Gold Haze is one of the most widely grown gold-foliage heather cultivars.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Gold Haze carries bright gold-yellow foliage year-round, contrasted by pure white flowers in late summer, one of the most widely grown gold-foliage heather cultivars since the mid-20th century. Its upright habit to about 18 inches and strong foliage color make it a dependable anchor plant for a heathland-style bed. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a compact, bushy shape.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Silver Knight is a classic grey-foliage cultivar long established in the UK heather trade.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Silver Knight carries downy silver-grey foliage topped by pale mauve-pink flowers, a classic grey-foliage cultivar valued especially for its distinctive winter texture when most heathers show green or seasonal color instead. Its compact mounding habit to about 12 inches suits a rock garden or acid-soil bed edge. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a tidy, compact mound.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Kinlochruel is a Scottish-raised double-white cultivar holding a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Kinlochruel is a Scottish-raised double white heather holding a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit, forming compact mounds to about 10 inches topped with light green foliage and double white flowers in late summer. Its award-winning status reflects consistently strong garden performance documented by the Heather Society. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a tidy, compact mound.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Darkness is a long-popular deep-purple-flowered cultivar common in the US nursery trade.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Darkness bears deep crimson-purple flowers densely packed along the spikes over dark green foliage, a long-popular cultivar common in the US nursery trade. Its low, spreading mound to about 10-12 inches makes an effective weed-suppressing ground cover in an acid-soil heathland bed. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain dense, compact growth.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Spring Cream is valued for its cream-colored new growth each spring.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Spring Cream is valued for its cream-white new spring foliage, which matures to green as the season progresses, topped by pale mauve flowers in late summer. The seasonal foliage color shift adds visual interest well before the flowering display begins each year. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a bushy, upright habit to about 12-15 inches.

common_name: Beoley Gold Heather (Gold Foliage, White Flowers)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Beoley Gold is a long-established gold-foliage cultivar related to the Beoley heather lineage.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Beoley Gold carries bright gold foliage year-round, paired with white flowers in late summer, a long-established cultivar within the broader Beoley heather lineage common in UK and European heather collections. Its upright, compact habit to about 12-15 inches gives it a tidier form than some spreading gold-foliage heathers. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain dense, bright growth.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Tib is a very old double-flowered cultivar, pre-1900, and one of the earliest-blooming heathers.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Tib is a very old heather cultivar, documented in cultivation before 1900 and recognized as a Heather Society reference plant, bearing double rose-purple flowers over dark green foliage. It blooms in midsummer, earlier than most other Calluna vulgaris cultivars, extending the heather garden's flowering season at the front end. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain a compact, upright habit to about 12 inches.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Wickwar Flame is documented in UK heather collections, with foliage color intensifying through winter.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Wickwar Flame carries orange-red foliage that intensifies to flame-red through winter, paired with mauve-pink flowers, a cultivar documented in UK heather collections though less common in US retail. Its low spreading habit to about 10 inches makes a good ground-covering companion to taller, upright heather cultivars. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain dense, colorful growth.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring into very acidic, lean soil in full sun; Mousehole is a Cornish-origin cultivar documented by the Heather Society.

directions: Plant in very acidic, lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Mousehole, named for the Cornish fishing village, bears deep ruby-red flowers over dark green foliage on a dense, low mound reaching only about 8 inches. It is documented by the Heather Society as a genuine, stable cultivar within UK nursery lists, though less mainstream in US retail than some classic heather cultivars. Shear lightly after flowering to maintain its tight, compact mound.
